hlni.insight: A task label alone does not reveal assessment methods or feedback types.
hlni.audienceGap: Students assume degree titles reveal the assessment methods and feedback types.
hlni.viewerChange: Viewers learn to evaluate a course by the feedback structure rather than the degree label.
hlni.support: The method separates three different pieces of information; it does not assume particular course content.
hlni.payoff: Using the unanswered cells to ask a precise question about the actual course or task before deciding.

creativeAngle: Evaluating courses via feedback structures rather than degree labels.
objective: Empower students to audit academic tasks.
targetAudience: +2 students seeking academic depth and well-supported course and career decisions

shots.name: The Title Trap
shots.visual: Split screen showing a B.Com and BBA brochure side-by-side. The student looks confused.
shots.dialogue: Choosing between B.Com and BBA? Don't let the degree title decide for you.
shots.cameraPerformance: Close-up on the student looking at screens, then turning to camera.

shots.name: The Task Audit
shots.visual: A worksheet appears on screen covering both degree sides. Text fills in.
shots.dialogue: Audit the task. Look here: Example: Task: Analyze Q3 financial variance. Graded by: ? Feedback available: ?
shots.onscreenText: Example: Task: Analyze Q3 financial variance. Graded by: ? Feedback available: ?
shots.cameraPerformance: Direct, clear shot of the graphic interface.

shots.name: The Concrete Question
shots.visual: Student holds the completed worksheet, pointing to the empty cells.
shots.dialogue: If you don't know the answer, ask this: What specific criteria do you use to grade this submission?
shots.onscreenText: What specific criteria do you use to grade this submission?
shots.cameraPerformance: Confident, direct address to the student.

productionNotes.camera: Stable tripod shots with clear graphic overlays.
productionNotes.editing: Rhythmic, allowing time to read the text.

creativeSummary.keyCreativeIdea: Shifting the focus from degree names to assessment feedback structures using a simple audit method.

selected.title: The Assessment Audit
selected.audienceGap: Students assume degree titles reveal the assessment methods and feedback types.
selected.hlni: A task label alone does not tell you what you must produce, what will be assessed, or what feedback you receive. Ask these as separate questions.
selected.viewerChange: Viewers learn to evaluate a course by the feedback structure rather than the degree label.
selected.concept: A student reviews two sample course task briefs to see that task labels are identical.
selected.device: Split-screen comparison of two task briefs with a shared audit worksheet overlay.
selected.support: The method separates three different pieces of information; it does not assume particular course content.
methodSteps: Ask what criterion is used to assess it.
Ask what feedback is available; mark unknown answers as questions.
selected.interpretationRule: Use the unanswered cells to ask a precise question about the actual course or task before deciding.
selected.visibleProof: A three-column question sheet turns one vague preference into a concrete unanswered question.
selected.payoff: Use the unanswered cells to ask a precise question about the actual course or task before deciding.
selected.limitations: This is a question-forming aid, not a degree ranking, aptitude test or prediction of success.

demonstration.input: Two identical task descriptions for a financial statement analysis.
demonstration.visibleInput: Example: Task: Analyze Q3 financial variance. Graded by: ? Feedback available: ?
demonstration.observation: Both tasks show identical labels but leave grading and feedback criteria as unknowns.
demonstration.nextQuestion: What specific criteria do you use to grade this submission?

comparedWith.hlni: An appealing option and an available option are different questions. Unknown requirements should be recorded as checks rather than assumed to be satisfied.
comparedWith.device: A checklist app interface where 'wishlist' items are marked as 'need to verify'.

comparedWith.hlni: The same total can result from different component values; an aggregate alone cannot tell you the underlying mix.
comparedWith.device: A digital block-stacking animation that reveals different segments.
